title: FATHER GOD, TAKE THE WEIGHT OFF MY SHOULDERS
text: Good morning precious people. Before we begin this powerful time in the presence of the Lord, I want you to do something very significant. Whatever platform you're watching this from, YouTube, Facebook, WhatsApp, I want you to share this prayer right now. Don't wait until after. Do it now. There is somebody in your contact list, somebody in your sphere of influence who is carrying a weight that is crushing them. They need this prayer. The Holy Spirit has orchestrated this moment, and you are a vessel of distribution for divine intervention. Share it now. Type I receive grace in the comment section as a point of contact for what God is about to do. Hallelujah. I want you to lift up your hands wherever you are. It doesn't matter if you're in your bedroom, your office, driving in your car safely, of course, lift up your hands onto the Lord. The Bible says in Psalm 134, "Lift up your hands in the sanctuary and bless the Lord." Your location has become a sanctuary because the presence of God is about to fill that space. I sense in my spirit that somebody has been carrying a burden that was never designed for your shoulders. Today is your day of divine relief. Glory to Jesus. Father, in the mighty name of Jesus, we come before your throne of grace. We honor you this morning. You are the lifter of our heads. You are the burden bearer. You are the one who said, "Come unto me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest." Lord, we take you at your word this morning. Every weight, every pressure, every burden that has been crushing your children, Father, we present them before you now in Jesus' mighty name. You know, the title of this ministration is powerful. Father, take the weight off my shoulders. And I want to establish something from the scripture. In Matthew chapter 11, verses 28 to 30, Jesus made a profound statement. He said, "Come unto me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me, for I am meek and lowly in heart, and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light." Now, notice the dimension of invitation that Jesus extended. He said, "Come unto me." Not come unto religion, not come unto programs, not come unto your own strength. Come unto me. There is a personal dimension to the ministry of Christ that many believers have not accessed. We have turned Christianity into a system when it was meant to be a relationship. And in relationship, there is exchange. You bring your burdens, he gives you his rest. You bring your weakness, he gives you his strength. You bring your confusion, he gives you his wisdom. Somebody say, "I receive divine exchange." Now, when we talk about weights and burdens, we must understand that there are different categories of weights that people carry. There are financial weights, debts that keep you awake at night, obligations you cannot meet, expectations from family members that are crushing your spirit. There are emotional weights, heartbreak, betrayal, disappointment, the pain of rejection, the agony of loss. There are physical weights, sickness in your body, chronic pain that has refused to leave, medical reports that have sentenced you to a life of limitation. But I want you to understand something profound this morning. There are also SPIRITUAL WEIGHTS. YES. THERE ARE weights that come from witchcraft assignments. There are weights that come from generational curses. There are weights that come from covenants that your ancestors entered into without your knowledge. The Bible speaks about the sin which does so easily beset us in Hebrews chapter 12. That word beset means to surround, to encircle, to trap. There are people who are literally trapped under weights that are not natural. They're spiritual. And the Lord is showing me somebody right now. You've been to hospitals, you've been to counselors, you've tried everything humanly possible, but nothing has worked because your situation is not medical, it's not psychological, it is spiritual. And until you address the spiritual root, the physical manifestation will continue to oppress you. But I prophesy to you today, every spiritual weight that has been assigned to crush your destiny, the Lord is breaking it now in the mighty name of Jesus. You see, when we look at the life of Christ, one of the most powerful miracles he performed was when he cast out a spirit of infirmity from a woman who had been bent over for 18 years. The Bible says in Luke chapter 13, that she was bound together and could in no wise lift herself up. FOR 18 YEARS. IMAGINE CARRYING A weight so heavy that it literally bends your physical frame. That woman could not stand straight. She could not look up. She had been going to the synagogue, participating in religious activities, but her condition remained unchanged. But when Jesus saw her, oh, I love this. When Jesus saw her, he called her to him. He didn't wait for her to cry out. He didn't wait for her to push through the crowd. He took the initiative. And he said to her, "Woman, thou art loose from thine infirmity." And immediately, the Bible says she was made straight and glorified God. Now, notice what Jesus said afterwards, when the religious leaders criticized him for healing on the Sabbath. He said, "Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan had bound low these 18 years, be loosed from this bond on the Sabbath day?" Jesus identified the source of her condition. It was Satan. It was a demonic weight that had been placed upon her to prevent her from standing in her full stature. And somebody here today, you are that woman. You are that man. For years, you've been bent over under the weight of depression, under the weight of poverty, under the weight of barrenness, under the weight of failure, but this is your Sabbath. This is your day of divine release. I prophesy to you, you will stand straight again. Your glory will be restored. Your joy will return. Your breakthrough will manifest in the mighty name of Jesus. Now, lift up your hands and pray with ME WITH VIOLENCE IN YOUR SPIRIT. WE'RE NOT PLAYING RELIGIOUS games this morning. Every satanic weight upon my life, break and scatter now in Jesus' name. Every demonic load that has been programmed to crush my destiny, I reject you. I denounce you. I destroy your power over my life in the mighty name of Jesus. Every covenant of heaviness, every agreement with sorrow, every partnership with depression, I break your hold over my life by the blood of Jesus. You spirit of heaviness. The Bible says in Isaiah 61:1-3 that God has given me the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness. I put on that garment now. I reject heaviness. I reject depression. I reject oppression. I receive joy. I receive peace. I receive divine rest in Jesus' mighty name. Every weight from my father's house, every weight from my mother's lineage, every generational burden that has been transferred to me, I am not the carrier. I am not the victim. I am the victor. The blood of Jesus speaks better things. That blood cancels every evil inheritance. That blood breaks every evil pattern. That blood delivers me from every generational curse in Jesus' name. Now, I want to take you deeper into the revelation of burden bearing. In Galatians chapter 6, verse 2, the Bible says, "Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ." But then in verse 5 of the same chapter, it says, "For every man shall bear his own burden." Now, this appears to be a contradiction, but it is actually a profound spiritual principle. There are burdens we are supposed to carry for one another out of love and compassion, the burden of intercession, the burden of supporting those who are weak, the burden of caring for the vulnerable. These are kingdom burdens, and they are light because grace accompanies them. But then there are burdens that we were never meant to carry, burdens of guilt for sins that have been forgiven, burdens of responsibility for other people's choices, burdens of fear about a future that God has already secured. Many believers are carrying weights that God never assigned to them. They are carrying the weight of other people's expectations. They are carrying the weight of cultural traditions that conflict with the word of God. They are carrying the weight of religious obligations that have no scriptural foundation, and these weights are crushing them. I remember the story of Elijah in 1 Kings chapter 19. After his powerful victory on Mount Carmel, where fire fell from heaven and consumed the sacrifice, Elijah ran from Jezebel's threat and sat under a juniper tree and asked God to take his life. He said, "It is enough. Now, oh Lord, take away my life." This mighty prophet, who had just called down fire from heaven, was now under such a weight of discouragement that he wanted to die. But notice what God did. God didn't rebuke him. God didn't tell him to have more faith. God ministered to his physical needs, first sent an angel to give him food and water. Then God took him to a mountain and spoke to him in a still, small voice. And finally, God gave him a new assignment and told him he was not alone. There were 7,000 others who had not bowed to Baal. What was God doing? God was removing the weight. The weight of isolation. You're not alone. The weight of failure. You still have an assignment. The weight of fear. I'm still with you. And Elijah rose up and continued his ministry with renewed strength. Somebody here you're like Elijah under that juniper tree. You fought battles, you've been faithful, but now you are exhausted. The enemy has spoken a word over your life that has placed a weight of discouragement on you. You are thinking, "What's the point? Nothing I do matters. I'm all alone in this fight." But the Lord is saying to you what he said to Elijah, "You are not alone. I have not forsaken you. Your assignment is not over. GET UP. EAT. REFRESH YOURSELF. THERE IS SOUND OF ABUNDANCE of rain. There is a mighty move of my spirit coming in your life." Can I pray for you right now? Father, in the name of Jesus, I pray for everyone who feels like Elijah under that juniper tree. Lord, they are exhausted, discouraged, ready to give up. But I prophesy fresh strength into their spirit right now. I prophesy renewed vision. I prophesy divine encouragement. Let your angels minister to them even now. Let them eat the bread of heaven. Let them drink from the rivers of living water. Restore their hope. Revive their passion. Reignite their purpose in Jesus' mighty name. Every weight of discouragement, break. Every spirit of suicide, leave. Every thought of giving up, I rebuke you in the name of Jesus. You shall not die. You shall live. You shall declare the works of the Lord. Your best days are ahead of you. Your greatest victories are coming. Your most powerful testimonies are about to be written in the mighty name of Jesus. Now, let me show you something else from the book of Exodus. When the children of Israel were in Egypt, they were under the weight of slavery. Pharaoh had tasked them with making bricks without straw. The Bible says in Exodus 5:13 that the taskmasters hastened them saying, "Fulfill your works, your daily tasks." They were under constant pressure, constant demands, constant weight. But when Moses came with a message of deliverance, Pharaoh increased their burden. He made their situation worse before it got better. And many believers don't understand this principle. Sometimes, when your deliverance is close, the enemy will increase the pressure. He will add more weight because he knows his time is short. If your situation has gotten more intense recently, if the pressure has increased, if more problems have piled up, don't panic. It's a sign that your breakthrough is near. The enemy is fighting harder because he knows God is about to do something significant in your life. Don't give up now. Don't quit now. Your Red Sea is about TO PART. YOUR EGYPT is about to release you. Your Pharaoh is about to let you go. I decree and declare every Pharaoh holding you in bondage, the Lord will deal with him. Every taskmaster adding to your burden, God will remove him. Every system designed to keep you in slavery, God will dismantle it. You are coming out. You are breaking free. You are crossing over to your promised land in the mighty name of Jesus. Now, when Jesus said in Matthew 11:28, "Come unto me, all ye that labor and are heavy laden." He used two different Greek words there. Labor speaks of exhausting work, toil, weariness from effort. Heavy laden speaks of being loaded down, carrying a heavy cargo, being burdened beyond capacity. Jesus was saying, "Whether you're exhausted from working or your crushed under a load that's too heavy, come to me." And then he said something remarkable, "Take my yoke upon you." Now, a yoke is an instrument used to join two animals together so they can pull a load together. When Jesus says, "Take my yoke," he's saying, "Let's carry this load together." You don't have to carry it alone anymore. I'll be yoked with you and we'll bear it together. And because he's the stronger partner in this yoke, he actually ends up carrying the greater portion of the weight. That's why he says, "My yoke is easy and my burden is light." Not because there's no burden, but because he's carrying most of it. When you're yoked with Jesus, your impossible becomes possible. Your unbearable becomes bearable. Your crushing weight becomes a light load. I remember counseling a young man who was carrying the weight of providing for his entire extended family. His father had died. And as the eldest son, cultural expectations demanded that he take care of everyone, his mother, his siblings, his uncles, his aunts, even distant relatives. He was working three jobs, barely sleeping, his health was failing, and he was drowning in debt. The weight was crushing him. And I told him, "Brother, God never called you to be the savior of your family. That's Jesus' job. Yes, you should help where you can, but you cannot carry what God has not graced you to carry. You need to give this weight to the Lord and let him show you what your actual responsibility is." When he finally released that weight to God in prayer, something shifted. Within months, other members of the family who had been depending on him found jobs. His mother received a pension that had been pending for years. Opportunities opened up that reduced his financial burden. Why? Because when he stopped carrying what God didn't give him to carry, grace came to handle the legitimate responsibilities that were actually his. Are you carrying weights that God never assigned to you? Are you trying to be the savior in situations where only Jesus can save? Are you taking responsibility for things that are beyond your control? It's time to release them. It's time to cast your cares upon him, for he cares for you. Look at Psalm 55:22. "Cast thy burden upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee. He shall never suffer the righteous to be moved." The word cast there is violent in the Hebrew. It means to throw, TO HURL, TO PITCH with force. God is not asking for a gentle handoff. He's saying, "Throw that burden at me. Get rid of it. Pitch it away from you with violence." And then he promises two things. He shall sustain thee. He will support you, hold you up, maintain you. He shall never suffer the righteous to be moved. You won't be shaken. You won't be toppled. You won't be crushed because the burden is no longer on you. It's on him. 1 Peter 5:5-7 says, "Casting all your care upon him, for he careth for you." All your care. Not some of it. Not the spiritual ones while you handle the practical ones. All of it. Every anxiety, every worry, every concern, every fear, every burden, cast it on him. Why? Because he cares for you. He's not indifferent to your pain. He's not ignoring your struggle. He cares deeply and personally about everything that affects you. Now, I want you to pray this prayer with me. And I want you to be specific. Don't pray general prayers. Identify the exact weight you're carrying and release it to God. Father, I come before you in the name of Jesus. I acknowledge that I have been carrying weights that are crushing me. Lord, I cannot carry them anymore. I am exhausted. I am overwhelmed. I am at the end of my strength. So, right now, by an act of my will, I cast these burdens upon you. I cast upon you the weight of this financial debt. I cast upon you the weight of this sickness. I cast upon you the weight of this broken relationship. I cast upon you the weight of this disappointed expectation. I cast upon you the weight of this family crisis. Lord, I throw these burdens at your feet. I will not pick them up again. I will not rehearse them in my mind. I will not meditate on them in fear. I have given them to you, and I receive your rest in exchange. I receive your peace. I receive your joy. I receive your strength in Jesus' mighty name. Now, let me speak to specific weights that people carry. The weight of guilt and condemnation. Romans 8:1 says, "There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus." If you've repented, if you've asked for forgiveness, then that sin is under the blood. Stop carrying guilt for something God has already forgiven. The enemy uses guilt to keep you bound, but the blood of Jesus has set you free. Receive that freedom now. The weight of unforgiveness. You're carrying the weight of what someone did to you years ago. You rehearse it. You meditate on it. You keep the pain fresh by refusing to forgive. But Ephesians 4:32 says, "Be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God, for Christ's sake, have forgiven you." That unforgiveness is a weight that's poisoning your spirit. Release it. Forgive them not because they deserve it, but because you deserve to be free. The weight of comparison and competition. You're carrying the burden of trying to measure up to others, trying to compete with their success, their achievements, their progress. But Galatians 6:4 says, "Let every man prove his own work, and then shall he have rejoicing in himself alone and not in another." God has a unique path for you. Your timing is different. Your journey is different. STOP COMPARING. STOP COMPETING. Run your own race. I pray for someone who has been carrying the weight of barrenness. You've been praying, believing, trusting God for a child, and the weight has been heavy. The questions from family members, the pressure from society, the disappointment every month is weighing you down. But I prophesy to you like the angel said to Sarah, is anything too hard for the Lord? At the time appointed you shall conceive. You shall carry. You shall birth. Your womb is opening now. Your reproductive system is RECEIVING DIVINE ALIGNMENT NOW. YOU SHALL be a joyful mother of children in Jesus' name. I pray for someone carrying the weight of a prodigal child. Your son, your daughter has walked away from God, and you blame yourself. The weight of guilt, the weight of shame, the weight of constant prayer without visible results is crushing you. But the Lord says to you what he said to the father of the prodigal son, your child shall come to himself. Your child shall return. Your child shall be restored. Don't give up on them. DON'T STOP PRAYING. THE ANGELS ARE WORKING. THE HOLY SPIRIT IS CONVICTING. THEY SHALL COME HOME. I PRAY FOR someone carrying the weight of business failure. You invested everything. You believed God, but it didn't work out the way you expected. The debt, the shame, the sense of failure is overwhelming. But Proverbs 24:16 says, a just man falleth seven times and riseth up again. This is not the end. This is a setup for a comeback. God is teaching you lessons in this valley that will make you powerful on your next mountain. Your setback is a setup for a supernatural comeback. Receive it now. You know, there's a powerful principle in Isaiah 61:3 that many believers miss. It says God gives us beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness. Notice that it's an exchange. You bring the ashes of your burned dreams. He gives you beauty. You bring the mourning of your losses. He gives you joy. You bring the spirit of heaviness. He gives you praise. But here's the key. You have to release what you're carrying in order to receive what he's giving. Some people want the beauty, but they won't let go of the ashes. They want the joy, but they're holding on to the mourning. They want praise, but they're comfortable with heaviness. You cannot receive what God has for you while holding on to what you have. It's like a child holding a broken toy, crying because it doesn't work anymore. The father is standing there with a brand new, better toy, saying, "Give me the broken one, and I'll give you this new one." But the child won't let go. He's emotionally attached to the broken toy. He's comfortable with his pain. He'd rather cry over what's broken than receive what's new. Some of you are like that child. God is saying, "Give me your pain. I'll give you peace. Give me your sickness. I'll give you health." GIVE ME YOUR POVERTY. I'll give you abundance. Give me your confusion. I'll give you clarity. But you won't let go. You're holding on to your problems like they're precious. Release them. Let them go. Receive what God has for you. Now, I'm going to pray a prayer of total release over your life, and I want you to receive it by faith. I want you to see those weights falling off your shoulders like heavy chains breaking. I want you to visualize yourself standing straight, shoulders back, head up, free. Father, in the mighty name of Jesus, I speak to every weight, every burden, every load that is upon your children right now. I COMMAND, BREAK. SCATTER. FALL OFF. IN JESUS' NAME. Every financial weight, break. Every emotional weight, scatter. Every spiritual weight, fall off. Every weight of sickness, leave. Every weight of barrenness, depart. Every weight of failure, release them. Every weight of oppression, lose them now. By the authority of the name of Jesus. By the power of his blood. By the anointing of the Holy Spirit, I declare freedom. I decree liberation. I pronounce deliverance. You are free. You are loose. You are released. In the mighty name of Jesus. Now, lift up your hands and receive. Don't analyze it. Don't question it. Just receive. Your shoulders are light. Your spirit is free. Your mind is clear. Your heart is at peace. You have been delivered. You have been set free. You have been made whole. In Jesus' mighty name. I decree that from today, you walk in supernatural rest. You walk in divine peace. You walk in holy joy. The weight is gone. The burden is lifted. The load is removed. You are free indeed. And whom the son sets free is free indeed. Give God praise. Give him glory. Give him honor. He has done it. He has answered. He has delivered. You are free, free, free in Jesus' mighty name. Amen and amen. Share this prayer with someone who needs it. Type, "I am free" in the comments. Give God praise for what he has done. Hallelujah. Glory to Jesus. We give you praise. Lord, we honor you. We magnify your name. You are faithful. You are powerful. You are mighty. Thank you, Jesus. Thank you, Lord. Thank you, Holy Spirit. We celebrate our freedom. We celebrate our deliverance. We celebrate our breakthrough. In Jesus' mighty name. Amen.
